title: $Rf^!$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p_0>0$ with $p_0\neq\ell$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). For each such scheme $T$, let $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(T,\Lambda)$ denote the bounded constructible derived category of module objects on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ over the coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_T$ pulled back from $\Lambda$ on the point ([sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]). Assume that the ambient derived pushforwards carry bounded constructible complexes to bounded constructible complexes, so they restrict to these categories as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors] and [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek].
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism and $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y)$ a compactification of $f$: $i$ is an open immersion, $p$ is proper, and $f=p\circ i$, with $Z$ also separated and of finite type over $k$. Assume that the restricted pushforward
$Rp_*\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)$
([sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors]) along the proper morphism $p$ has a right adjoint. For
every proper $p$ this holds when $\Lambda$ is $\underline E$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite),
$\underline{\cO}_E$ ($E\subseteq\Qlb$ finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$; [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring])
or $\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]). Let $Rp^!$ be a chosen right adjoint of
$Rp_*$, and let $i^*=Li^*$ be the restricted pullback, which is right adjoint to $i_!$. Define

$$
Rf^!_c:=i^*\circ Rp^!\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda),
$$

and $Rf^!:=Rf^!_{c_f}$ for the chosen compactification $c_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], under
the assumption for $p_f$. The composite of the adjunctions $i_!\dashv i^*$ and $Rp_*\dashv Rp^!$ is
an adjunction

$$
Rf_!^c\dashv Rf^!_c,
$$

with $Rf_!^c=Rp_*\circ i_!$ the lower shriek of [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek]. In particular
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, so $Rf_!$ is a left adjoint and $Rf^!$ is a right adjoint. The functor $Rp^!$
is an abstract choice together with its adjunction, determined up to a unique natural
isomorphism compatible with the chosen adjunction counits, and is used only through the
adjunction. The functor $Rf^!$ is constructed directly on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$, so no separate
statement that it preserves constructibility is needed.

proof.text: Choose a right adjoint $Rp^!$ together with its adjunction $Rp_*\dashv Rp^!$, as the hypothesis permits. The three asserted coefficient cases use respectively [lem-sfb-dc-proper-pushforward-left-adjoint-e], [lem-sfb-dc-proper-pushforward-left-adjoint-oe] and [lem-sfb-dc-proper-pushforward-left-adjoint-qlbar]. Their hypotheses apply to the proper leg $p\colon Z\to Y$ of the compactification: both schemes and the morphism belong to the standing setting. Each gives a right adjoint on the bounded constructible categories themselves, with exactly the coefficient ring in its statement. No existence assertion for a general condensed ring is used.

source.place: right-adjoint hypothesis and the three coefficient cases

proof.text: The restricted pullback $Li^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors] is a functor from $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)$ to $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$. Define $Rf^!_c(K)=Li^*(Rp^!K)$, and for a morphism $a\colon K\to K'$ define $Rf^!_c(a)=Li^*(Rp^!(a))$. These formulas respect identities and compositions because each factor is a functor. The output is bounded constructible because the codomain of each factor is already the indicated bounded constructible category. This defines the displayed composite without choosing any additional object or asserting preservation by an ambient exceptional inverse image.

source.place: displayed definition of the exceptional inverse image attached to a compactification; final sentence

proof.text:
By [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction], the open immersion $i$ gives $i_!\dashv Li^*$ on the restricted categories. For $M\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$ and $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)$, compose the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_*i_!M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_!M,Rp^!K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,Li^*Rp^!K).$$
This is the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] (Stacks Tag 0DV0, categories.tex, lemma-compose-counits). If $\eta^i,\varepsilon^i$ and $\eta^p,\varepsilon^p$ are the units and counits of the two input adjunctions, its unit at $M$ is $Li^*(\eta^p_{i_!M})\circ\eta^i_M$ and its counit at $K$ is $\varepsilon^p_K\circ Rp_*(\varepsilon^i_{Rp^!K})$. Thus it has precisely the required unit, counit and triangle identities. Its left functor is $Rf_!^c=Rp_*\circ i_!$ by [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek], and its right functor is the composite just defined, so $Rf_!^c\dashv Rf^!_c$.

source.place: Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits; specialized to the two adjunctions in the blueprint definition

proof.text: Take $c=c_f$, the compactification fixed in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], using the right-adjoint hypothesis for its proper leg $p_f$. Define $Rf^!$ to be the composite of step 2 with this choice. By [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek], $Rf_!$ is $Rf_!^{c_f}$ with the same choice. Substitution in step 3 gives $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$. Having this adjunction is exactly what it means for $Rf_!$ to be a left adjoint and $Rf^!$ to be a right adjoint.

source.place: chosen compactification and the concluding adjunction

proof.text: Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to $F=Rp_*$ and two choices $G,J$ of its right adjoint with their adjunctions. The comparison at $K$ is the transpose $\gamma_K\colon GK\to JK$ of the first counit, characterized by $\varepsilon^J_K\circ Rp_*(\gamma_K)=\varepsilon^G_K$. That statement gives naturality, an inverse, and uniqueness among counit-compatible comparisons. This is the unique isomorphism of right adjoints meant in the definition. Applying the functor $Li^*$ to this isomorphism also compares the two composites. Only the adjunction data of $Rp^!$ enter this construction, so no extra construction or constructibility claim about an ambient $Rp^!$ is required.

source.place: categorical statement, applied to the proper restricted pushforward
